title: The Gluten Fragment That Changed Its Charge — Celiac TG2 Cys277 Gln→Glu Deamidation, HLA-DQ2.5 Lysβ71 Pocket (1S9V), Irreversible ZED1227 Active-Site Trapping & Gluten-Challenge Biopsy Trials

teenKit.tldr: A microscopic electrical charge change on a single dietary gluten fragment tricks the immune system into attacking the body's own small intestine. Cutting-edge drugs are now being engineered to intercept this atomic-level molecular crime.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how a tiny protein swap causes total-body exhaustion proves that massive human health struggles often start down at the invisible atomic scale.
keyTakeaways: Tissue transglutaminase 2 (TG2) chemically alters gluten by turning neutral glutamine into negatively charged glutamate.
The immune system's HLA-DQ2.5 receptor uses a specific positively charged pocket (Lysβ71) to anchor these newly negative gluten fragments, triggering an immune attack.
ZED1227 is an innovative experimental drug that acts as a targeted inhibitor to trap the active site of TG2 and halt the destructive autoimmune chain reaction.

vocab.meaning: A chemical reaction that strips a specific group off a molecule, which in celiac disease adds a negative electrical charge to gluten.
An enzyme in our gut that accidentally alters gluten fragments, making them magnetic to the immune system.
An immune system protein receptor featuring a positively charged pocket that tightly grips negatively charged gluten.
A pharmacological drug designed to physically block and trap the active site of the TG2 enzyme to prevent intestinal damage.

quiz.question: What is the primary atomic change that tissue transglutaminase 2 (TG2) makes to gluten?
options: It adds a positive charge to the molecule
It turns neutral glutamine into negatively charged glutamate
It completely destroys the protein structure into amino acids
It coats the gluten in protective antibodies
quiz.explanation: TG2 chemically modifies gluten by deamidating glutamine into a negatively charged glutamate, which starts the immune cascade.

quiz.question: Why does the HLA-DQ2.5 immune receptor bind so aggressively to modified gluten?
options: Its Lysβ71 pocket is positively charged and attracts the newly negative gluten fragment
It mistakes gluten for an invading bacterial cell wall
It physically digests the gluten into pure energy
It repels all other nutrients except gluten
quiz.explanation: Opposites attract: the positive charge of the receptor's pocket forms a high-affinity anchor with the newly negative gluten.

quiz.question: What is the goal of the ZED1227 drug evaluated in clinical trials?
options: To replace the patient's entire small intestine lining
To permanently boost the body's total IgA levels
To act as an active-site inhibitor that traps and blocks TG2 enzyme activity
To speed up the digestion of complex carbohydrates
quiz.explanation: ZED1227 is a targeted covalent inhibitor designed to shut down TG2 so it can no longer alter gluten and trigger immune destruction.
